AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why are diseased plants not added to compost? (1 mark)
   A. They make the heap too tall
   B. They rot too slowly to count
   C. They are too heavy
   D. The disease can spread to the crops later

2. Which of these is a green material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Dry leaves
   B. Dry maize stalks
   C. Fresh cut grass
   D. Straw

3. Which crop is likely to be eaten by birds? (1 mark)
   A. Rocks
   B. Compost
   C. Firewood
   D. Ripening millet

4. What is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal kept in a house
   B. An animal that lives freely in nature
   C. An animal sold in shops
   D. An animal kept for milk

5. How long may carrot seeds take to sprout? (1 mark)
   A. One day
   B. One year
   C. One hour
   D. One to three weeks

6. Why are carrots not transplanted? (1 mark)
   A. They have no roots
   B. They are too large
   C. They grow in water
   D. Moving damages the root and makes it crooked

7. What is transplanting? (1 mark)
   A. Harvesting
   B. Sowing seeds directly
   C. Making compost
   D. Moving young plants from a nursery to the field

8. What does sowing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting a crop
   B. Watering a crop
   C. Storing seeds
   D. Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow

9. How do you know millet is ready to harvest? (1 mark)
   A. The seeds are wet
   B. The plant flowers
   C. The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   D. The plants are green and soft

10. What should be done with extra fruits? (1 mark)
   A. Throw them away
   B. Bury them
   C. Leave them to rot
   D. Share or sell them and avoid wasting

11. Which is a woody tree fruit in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Raspberry
   B. Kiwi
   C. Tree tomato
   D. Grapes

12. Why should young fruit trees be watered in dry weather? (1 mark)
   A. Water kills them
   B. They do not need water
   C. Their roots are small and cannot reach much water
   D. Water makes fruit sour

13. Why should the soil be firmed around a newly planted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To remove air spaces and hold the roots
   C. To make the plant fall
   D. To dry the roots

14. Which of these is a fruit crop? (1 mark)
   A. Cabbage
   B. Sukuma wiki
   C. Spinach
   D. Guava

15. Which group of animals is called poultry? (1 mark)
   A. Sheep and goats
   B. Zebras and giraffes
   C. Cows and bulls
   D. Chickens, ducks and turkeys

16. Which animal browses on leaves and shoots from bushes? (1 mark)
   A. Rabbit only
   B. Hen
   C. Goat
   D. Duck

17. What is a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. A meal with foods from all the main groups in the right amounts
   B. A meal with only one kind of food
   C. A very large meal
   D. A meal of only sweets

18. Which of these meals is balanced? (1 mark)
   A. Chips only
   B. Tea and bread only
   C. Soda and sweets
   D. Ugali, beans and sukuma wiki

19. What is one way to choose foods for a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Pick only cheap food
   B. Pick one or more foods from each group
   C. Pick only sweet food
   D. Pick only your favourite food

20. Which of these is an energy-giving food? (1 mark)
   A. Orange
   B. Spinach
   C. Ugali
   D. Fish

21. Which is an advantage of boiling? (1 mark)
   A. It needs no oil
   B. It always burns food
   C. It makes food black
   D. It needs deep oil

22. How can you tell that water is boiling? (1 mark)
   A. The water is cold
   B. Big bubbles rise quickly and steam comes off
   C. The water is blue
   D. The water is still

23. How do you test if boiled potatoes are cooked? (1 mark)
   A. They float
   B. They turn green
   C. A fork goes in easily
   D. They are still very hard

24. What is shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking in a small amount of hot oil in a pan
   B. Cooking in water
   C. Cooking in a lot of deep oil
   D. Baking in an oven

25. Which way should you open a lid on a hot pot? (1 mark)
   A. Straight toward your face
   B. Under water
   C. Fast and close
   D. Away from your face

26. About how long should you rub hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. About 20 seconds
   B. Not at all
   C. About 5 minutes
   D. About 1 second

27. Why should fingernails be kept short? (1 mark)
   A. Germs and worm eggs hide under long nails
   B. Short nails grow faster
   C. Long nails are heavy
   D. Nails are food

28. What should you use to brush your teeth? (1 mark)
   A. A knife
   B. A comb
   C. A toothbrush and toothpaste
   D. A cloth soaked in oil

29. When should you wash your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Only on Sunday
   B. Only after school ends
   C. Never
   D. Before eating and after using the toilet

30. What should you use to wash your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Mud
   B. Only dry cloth
   C. Dirty water
   D. Soap and clean water

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three benefits of eating a balanced meal. (3 marks)

32. Name two problems that can attack ripe fruits. (2 marks)

33. Give three signs that fruit is ripe, naming the fruit. (3 marks)

34. State the functions of roots, leaves and flowers in a fruit tree. (3 marks)

35. What should you do after cooking to keep the kitchen safe and clean? (2 marks)

36. Describe how to prepare a class talk about one domestic animal. (4 marks)

37. Explain how to make a meal of boiled potatoes and fried egg balanced. (3 marks)

38. Give three mistakes to avoid when sowing tiny seeds. (3 marks)

39. Explain why a tippy tap is useful in a school without a tap. (3 marks)

40. Why do some fruit trees take longer to give fruit than others? (3 marks)

41. List four basic needs of domestic animals. (4 marks)

42. Give three reasons why nails should be kept short and clean. (3 marks)

43. Why should fruit be washed before it is eaten? (2 marks)

44. Why should personal items like towels not be shared? (2 marks)

45. Explain two mistakes that can spoil a newly planted fruit tree and how to avoid them. (4 marks)

46. Explain the meaning of personal hygiene. (2 marks)

47. Explain how good personal hygiene helps prevent diseases such as diarrhoea. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — The disease can spread to the crops later
   Disease germs may survive and infect crops when the compost is used.

2. C — Fresh cut grass
   Green materials are fresh and wet, such as fresh grass, peelings and fresh dung.

3. D — Ripening millet
   Birds eat ripening grain such as millet and sorghum.

4. B — An animal that lives freely in nature
   Wild animals are not kept by people.

5. D — One to three weeks
   Carrot seeds are slow, so be patient.

6. D — Moving damages the root and makes it crooked
   The carrot root is the food, so it must grow straight.

7. D — Moving young plants from a nursery to the field
   Transplanting means moving seedlings.

8. D — Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow
   Sowing is planting seeds.

9. C — The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   Ripe grain is hard and dry.

10. D — Share or sell them and avoid wasting
   Extra fruits can earn money or feed others.

11. C — Tree tomato
   Tree tomato and guava are woody.

12. C — Their roots are small and cannot reach much water
   Young trees are easily stressed by drought.

13. B — To remove air spaces and hold the roots
   Air pockets dry out roots.

14. D — Guava
   Guava is a fruit.

15. D — Chickens, ducks and turkeys
   Poultry means birds kept for eggs and meat.

16. C — Goat
   Goats browse on shrubs.

17. A — A meal with foods from all the main groups in the right amounts
   A balanced meal includes energy, body-building and protective foods.

18. D — Ugali, beans and sukuma wiki
   It includes all three groups.

19. B — Pick one or more foods from each group
   A balanced meal includes all three groups.

20. C — Ugali
   Ugali is a starchy staple.

21. A — It needs no oil
   Boiled food is low in fat.

22. B — Big bubbles rise quickly and steam comes off
   These are signs of boiling.

23. C — A fork goes in easily
   Soft potatoes are ready.

24. A — Cooking in a small amount of hot oil in a pan
   Shallow frying uses a thin layer of oil.

25. D — Away from your face
   Steam can burn.

26. A — About 20 seconds
   This is long enough to clean properly.

27. A — Germs and worm eggs hide under long nails
   Clean short nails prevent infection.

28. C — A toothbrush and toothpaste
   These clean teeth safely.

29. D — Before eating and after using the toilet
   These are key times.

30. D — Soap and clean water
   Soap removes germs.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives energy, helps the body to grow and repair, and protects from illness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fruit flies, birds or monkeys (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Passion fruit turns purple or yellow and wrinkles; guava turns yellowish and smells sweet; pawpaw turns yellow or orange and gives when pressed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with fruit.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the tree and take in water; leaves make food using sunlight; flowers form fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put out the fire or switch off the gas, wash and store utensils and wipe the working area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fire or gas, 1 mark for cleaning.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose an animal; collect pictures; list its uses and care; practise speaking clearly; present and answer questions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes give energy and the egg gives protein. Add vegetables such as spinach or tomato for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group named.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Leaving big lumps in the seedbed, sowing too deep, sowing too thick without thinning, or watering strongly (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: It saves water, it can be made cheaply from a container, and children do not touch the container with dirty hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Big trees such as mango grow slowly and need years before flowering, while pawpaw and passion fruit are small plants that fruit within about a year.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for slow trees, fast plants, and reason of size or type.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean water, enough feed, clean shelter, health care and kind handling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each need.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Germs hide under nails, worm eggs are found there, and long nails can scratch and cause injury.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remove dirt and germs so it is safe to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for germs or safety.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Germs and skin infections spread through them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for infection.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Burying the graft joint under the soil, plant with joint above the ground; not watering in dry weather, water regularly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake and 1 for each solution.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keeping our own body clean to stay healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for health.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Washing hands removes germs before they reach the mouth. Safe water and clean food stop germs entering the body. Using the toilet and washing hands afterwards stops germs from spreading.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.
